> 遯。亨。小利貞。

Hexagram 33 is usually translated "retreat," and the character's dictionary sense rules out most of what that word suggests.

## 遯 is 遷 — moving one's position

A version fact first: the old text of the 易 has 遯; the received text has 遁.

說文: 遯，遷也 — 遷 is to move, to shift one's place.

逃 is a different word.

And that distinction is the whole chapter's fixed point: 遯 is to move one's position, not to run.

遷 is active, measured, and reversible. 逃 is passive, panicked, and indiscriminate about where it goes.

The 彖 says 與時行也 — walk with the time. Which is 遷: shift your position according to the season.

## 遯尾

初六 遯尾，厲，勿用有攸往.

尾: the end, the back. Slow to move when the time for moving has come, so the retreat falls at the tail.

厲, and do not go anywhere. The line's problem is timing, not courage: it is the one who leaves last.

## 執之用黃牛之革，莫之勝說

六二: bound with the hide of a yellow ox, and nothing can loosen it.

黃 is the colour of the centre; ox hide is tough and clinging. 說 is 脫, to slip free.

莫之勝說 — nothing can pull it off.

So: hold on with what is central and tough, and it cannot be untied. And this is the line that does not retreat — it stays, bound. Which the hexagram treats as a good position, because 遯's subject is a time when some should move and some should hold.

## 系遯

九三: tied and retreating.

系 is a tether. The heart still holds some name, some profit, some obligation — so it wants to leave and is held.

有疾厲; 畜臣妾，吉.

Sickness and danger. And then: keeping servants and concubines — good.

The second half is strange until it is read structurally: the line can manage what is close and dependent on it, but cannot make the large withdrawal. Its competence is domestic; its failure is public.

## 好遯 / 嘉遯 / 肥遯

好: genuinely glad to withdraw, not driven out. 君子吉，小人否 — the difference is whether the withdrawal is chosen or just an escape.

嘉: fine, well-timed. Withdrawal at exactly the right moment, praise contained in it.

肥: ample, roomy. The body and mind at ease, no encumbrance, going far off.

(肥 also has a reading as 飛, "flying away." Both readings produce the same sense — no drag — and this book keeps both.)

So the top of the hexagram is graded by how much is left behind: a tether, a choice, a timing, an emptiness.

## 不惡而嚴

The 象: 君子以遠小人，不惡而嚴.

Not showing aversion, and severe.

嚴 here is not severity toward others — it is the severity of one's own boundary. Do not display dislike; do not dissolve the line either.

Which is the practical craft of 遯 in a room you cannot leave: the position moves, the temperature does not.

## The test

Take a situation you are thinking of leaving. Ask which word describes what you are about to do: 遷 or 逃. Then ask which of the four grades you are at, and specifically whether the withdrawal was chosen or forced. The hexagram's first two verdicts are both about that distinction, not about the leaving itself.
